purpose: Remove the unrelated whole-Vault count from search results; retain returned-record counts, explicit bounded coverage and completed empty-search status. Test the contract without output filters or inference-policy changes.
comparison: Each arm uses production cache settings qualified before this study. Apple uses system-managed sampling. Baselines are frozen original-contract workers; candidates restore the original memory-save prompt before freezing.
acceptance: Tool output must match actual results, never conflate whole-Vault counts, records and URLs, preserve full-record and empty-result behavior, and avoid new write/ownership defects. Review every answer and call against evidence; report complete task scores and observed regressions separately, including unrelated misses. A deterministic contract repair is not a claim that all count hallucinations are solved.
limits: One Mac, reused regression scenarios, implementing-agent review without blinding. No leaderboard update or model-family generalization.
constraints: No corpus edits after execution starts
No concurrent inference and builds/performance checks
